task: Write one sentence of your own using the word sanguine. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know sanguine should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Down three games to one, the manager stayed oddly sanguine, penciling in the same lineup and predicting a comeback by Sunday.
Wishful is wanting without expecting — milder than sanguine, which genuinely believes the good news is coming.
Blithe goes further than sanguine — the sanguine planner expects things to work out and still checks the forecast; the blithe one has stopped checking anything at all.

Hopeful means wanting and wishing for the good outcome — hope reaches for good news but stops short of forecasting it. Sanguine goes further and expects: cheerful, settled confidence that things will come right. Hope crosses its fingers; sanguine checks the calendar and smiles.

Confident means sure of the outcome — certainty, with or without a smile. Sanguine adds the good cheer and makes the whole outlook a temperament: a sanguine person meets bad news still cheerfully expecting things to come right. You can be grimly confident; nobody is grimly sanguine.
expecting the worst, and glum about it
convinced the bad outcome is the likely one

Latin sanguis, 'blood,' built almost nothing else you'd meet in an ordinary English day — its other descendants (sanguinary, consanguinity) are rare legal and literary visitors. Learn sanguine on its own, and let the four-humors story hold it in memory.
Sanguine means optimistic, cheery.
The startup's servers crashed on launch morning, but its founder stayed sanguine on the all-hands call: 'We patch tonight, we relaunch Friday, and in a year this is the story we tell at parties.'
Sanguine is optimism as a temperament — confident good cheer that holds up in bad weather.
Hopeful people want the good outcome; sanguine people expect it.
Medieval doctors thought the mood came from a healthy supply of blood, and the word still carries that ruddy, unbothered glow.
Sanguine is the polished word for durable optimism — analysts are sanguine about earnings, captains stay sanguine in storms.
It is steadier than upbeat (in this unit's reference list) and roomier than hopeful: hope wants, sanguine expects.
In this unit's weather system, sanguine is the climate while elated is a single sunny burst.

Ilsa, who had led eleven expeditions on the mountain, remained perfectly sanguine.

'High pressure is coming,' she said.
